tasks.instruction: Refill is needed when ten times the level is at most the capacity; a level of exactly one tenth must also trigger a refill.
tasks.note: le versus lt at exactly one tenth; adding 1 to the capacity wraps at the maximum.

tasks.instruction: The function should return k times (1 + 2 + 3 + 4): the step weights must run from 1 to 4, not from 0 to 3.
tasks.note: weights 1..4; the wrong edit runs 5 steps.

tasks.instruction: Return the 4-bit field held in bits 4 through 7 of the input (bit 0 is the lowest).
Return the array with its last slot overwritten by the value from its first slot.
tasks.note: source index 0, destination 3; index 4 wraps to 0.

tasks.instruction: A motion passes when at least three of the four votes are nonzero.
The heater should run only when it is cold and it is not night.
The odometer shows five digits, so the new reading must roll over to 0 when it reaches 100000.
Experience levels up when the total reaches 100: return the total minus 100 and true, otherwise the total and false.
Days are now numbered with 0 as Sunday and 6 as Saturday; the result should be true only for those two days.
Drop the oldest (first) sample, move the others one place toward the front, and put the new value in the last slot.
tasks.note: three indices each shift by one.

tasks.instruction: Entries at odd positions are withdrawals and entries at even positions are deposits, and the account opens with the second argument as its balance; return whether it ever went below zero.
tasks.note: parity and initial balance both change.

tasks.instruction: Pack the colour as 5-6-5: red in bits 11-15, a 6-bit green in bits 5-10, blue in bits 0-4.
tasks.note: red shift and green width both change.

tasks.instruction: The rate argument is now given in tenths of a percent (so 25 means 2.5 per cent per period); keep the three periods and the rounding down.
The calibrated reading should be four times the raw reading plus three.
The door must stay shut once three or more failed attempts have been recorded, even with the right code.
Count how many of the elements after the first are equal to the first element; the first element itself must not be counted.
